transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-21 11:00 PT, duration ~48 minutes. Attendees listed in metadata.

[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lina from Redwood, AE on this account, with Samir our solutions engineer and Maya from customer success. How's everyone?
[00:05] Dr. Karen Liu: Hi Lina, good thanks. Excited to get into the POC scoping.
[00:08] Miguel Ramos: Hey. We'll try to keep it focused.
[00:11] Samir Patel: Great. Quick agenda: align success criteria, confirm workload sizing and golden prompt plan, agree on benchmarks and timeline.
[00:20] Priya Singh: For context, we're using the model for clinical note summarization and triage suggestion. Primary concerns are hallucinations and strict formatting for EHR ingestion.
[00:30] Lina Park: Perfect. On success criteria, we have three buckets — correctness/clinical accuracy, hallucination rate (we typically measure hallucinations per 1k outputs), and format adherence (JSON schema pass rate). Do those cover it?
[00:40] Dr. Karen Liu: Yes. Also add latency SLO for triage since it plugs into triage queues — we need under 700ms p50 end-to-end ideally.
[00:50] Samir Patel: Noted. We'll record latency both cold and warm, and p50/p95. For quality, suggest we define thresholds: clinical accuracy >= 92% on golden set, hallucination rate <= 1% on sampled outputs, and format adherence >= 98%. Thoughts?
[01:10] Evan Brooks: From security side, those are fine, but format adherence is critical — malformed JSON causes downstream failures. Also add audit logs and encryption in transit at rest requirement — we need SOC2 evidence.
[01:25] Lina Park: We'll send SOC2 and ISO docs as part of the security packet. On the POC mode, you mentioned preference for VPC — is that mandatory for the POC or for production?
[01:35] Miguel Ramos: For POC, hosted is fine if data is synthetic/anonymized; for real PHI, we'd need private VPC. We'll likely start with de-id data for initial runs.
[01:45] Samir Patel: OK. For the quality eval plan, here's our proposed approach: 1) Golden prompts: customer supplies ~200 high-priority prompts per use case with expected outputs and edge-case annotations. 2) Regression tests: a larger corpus (~2k prompts) sampled from logs and synthetic cases for continuous checks. 3) Hallucination checks via fact extraction and clinician review on sampled outputs. 4) Format checks against a strict JSON schema.
[02:10] Priya Singh: 200 golden prompts — is that enough? For edge cases we may want more.
[02:15] Samir Patel: 200 is the baseline for the initial POC; we can expand after first round. The golden set needs high-quality labeled expected outputs so scoring is meaningful.
[02:25] Dr. Karen Liu: For scoring, do you do string match or semantic similarity? Our concern is that slight wording differences still may be clinically equivalent.
[02:33] Samir Patel: Good point. We recommend hybrid scoring: structured fields (e.g., diagnosis codes, severity levels) use exact match; free-text summaries use a combination of ROUGE/BLEU and a clinical similarity model (embedding-based cosine similarity) with human spot checks. We'll provide the scoring script.
[02:50] Lina Park: We'll also include a hallucination detector where we flag extraneous fact mentions compared to a known facts set; these flags go into the scoring as penalties.
[02:58] Miguel Ramos: For the known facts set, we can supply canonical patient vitals and medication lists per example.
[03:05] Samir Patel: Great. Workload sizing — Miguel, can you share expected QPS and typical prompt lengths?
[03:12] Miguel Ramos: Right now peak is about 25 QPS with bursts to 50, average prompt length ~600 tokens, responses ~200 tokens. Payloads include metadata and attachments pointers but not full notes.
[03:25] Samir Patel: That's helpful. For benchmarking we'll simulate 50 concurrent QPS, and run experiments across model families and quantization profiles. We'll capture latency, token cost, and quality metrics.
[03:40] Priya Singh: How long does a benchmark run take? We need to schedule with our SRE windows.
[03:45] Samir Patel: Each model/variant run for the 2k corpus should take ~2-3 hours including warmup. If we run five variants, budget a day. We can parallelize on Redwood Dedicated capacity to compress time.
[04:00] Dr. Karen Liu: Can you summarize the benchmarks you'll run?
[04:05] Samir Patel: Sure — baseline open model (non-quantized), quantized 4-bit variant, a faster small model for latency vs cost tradeoff, and an ensemble fallback run. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on golden set, hallucination rate, format pass rate.
[04:30] Lina Park: Timeline proposal: golden prompts and expected outputs by 04/24, Redwood invoices small POC credit/account setup by 04/23, benchmark runs week of 04/27, results and walkthrough 05/01. Is that acceptable?
[04:45] Miguel Ramos: Yes that works for us.
[04:48] Evan Brooks: Security checklist — we'll need SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration for production. For the POC, at minimum secure API keys and audit logs to our SIEM by the benchmark phase.
[05:05] Lina Park: We'll include SSO guidance and KMS integration notes; for POC we can forward logs to a temporary endpoint.
[05:12] Priya Singh: On regression tests, how do we ensure we catch formatting regressions?
[05:18] Samir Patel: We'll run schema validation in CI — the regression corpus will be scored automatically and any JSON parse failures will be flagged as critical. We'll include checks that ensure required fields exist and values are in allowed ranges.
[05:35] Dr. Karen Liu: About hallucinations, can you show an example of how you annotate and score them?
[05:40] Samir Patel: Yes — example: model invents a medication not in the meds list — that's a hallucination. We tag hallucinations and assign severity weight (critical if leads to action, minor otherwise). Scoring is subtractive: total score minus weighted hallucination penalties.
[05:58] Priya Singh: Who on our side will do clinician spot checks? We need to allocate 4 hours per 200 golden prompts?
[06:05] Dr. Karen Liu: I can allocate 6 clinician-hours initial review and then ad-hoc spot checks. We'll try to expand if needed.
[06:12] Lina Park: Good. On deliverables: we'll share a draft quality eval plan and a template for golden prompt labeling by Friday 04/23. You provide samples and the larger regression corpus by 04/24. Then we run benchmarks and sync on 05/01.
[06:25] Miguel Ramos: One more thing — cost reporting. We'll need per-run cost estimates.
[06:30] Samir Patel: We'll provide cost per 1k tokens and estimated monthly cost at your QPS and token distribution. Also suggestions on batching/kv-cache settings to lower cost.
[06:45] Priya Singh: For formatting, can Redwood enforce strict JSON and return error codes if schema fails? We want to fail fast rather than downstream silently accept.
[06:55] Samir Patel: Yes, we can configure route-level schema enforcement and return HTTP 422 on schema violations. We can add a 'format_enforced' flag in the POC routes.
[07:05] Dr. Karen Liu: Is there a recommended threshold for hallucination that would block go/no-go?
[07:10] Lina Park: Typically customers set <1% hallucination on golden set as a pass. Given clinical risk, you might choose a stricter threshold; we can make that configurable.
[07:20] Miguel Ramos: Let's propose 0.5% for critical outputs, else 1% overall.
[07:25] Priya Singh: Agreed.
[07:28] Samir Patel: Ok we'll encode that as suggested thresholds in the plan.
[07:32] Lina Park: Any other risks?
[07:35] Evan Brooks: Data residency — for production we may need EU region. For POC not critical, but flagging.
[07:42] Samir Patel: Noted. Redwood supports region pinning for Dedicated/Private.
[07:48] Priya Singh: About regression cadence — after POC, how frequently do you recommend runs? Weekly?
[07:55] Samir Patel: For high-change environments, nightly synthetic regression and weekly full runs is common; for you, weekly full runs should be fine initially.
[08:05] Dr. Karen Liu: If we hit a regression in quality, do you support automatic rollback?
[08:10] Samir Patel: Yes — Redwood Console supports rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model versions on quality regressions, we can show this in the demo.
[08:20] Lina Park: Recap of action items and owners in chat now. We'll also share the draft plan and golden prompt template by Friday. Any final questions?
[08:30] Miguel Ramos: No, that's it from us. Thanks.
[08:33] Dr. Karen Liu: Thanks everyone.
[08:35] Lina Park: Thanks, talk soon.
